title: The Orbit Equation
protagonist: Devon Achebe, gameplay camera engineer, boss-fight cutscene team
primary_metric: percent of the frame the boss occupies, averaged over the fight, per millisecond of per-frame camera-path computation

options.A: The Fixed-Radius Orbit -- a constant-radius circular camera path around the boss, computed in polar coordinates, cheap to run and comfortably clear of the arena wall
options.B: The Variable-Radius Push-In -- a polar curve whose radius shrinks during the boss's telegraphed attack for a more dramatic frame, at a higher per-frame compute cost and a tighter clearance from the arena wall

sensitivity_disclosure.justification: Per-frame compute cost (MA3) is a studio-internal engineering estimate; no public source measures any specific studio's own per-operation camera-code timing on its own hardware, and this cannot be known in advance by further research -- it is a forecast-class unknown, not a lookup. Both +/-50% flexes breach the SPEC 20% cap; +50% also flips the winner to B.

Same basis as cost_A (MA4): a studio-internal per-operation engineering estimate no public source publishes, irreducible to further research. Both +/-50% flexes breach the SPEC 20% cap; -50% also flips the winner to B.

Push-in depth (MA6) is a production/animation-direction choice made scene by scene; no public source sets this value for any specific game, and it cannot be looked up, only decided. A +50% flex (6 -> 9) flips the winner to B at a 4.98% margin -- this is exactly the case's own Twist, disclosed in case.json.balance.twist_effect and FACILITATOR.md, not a hidden instability. A -50% flex does not flip the winner and stays under the 20% cap.

sensitivity_disclosure_note: MA1 (clipping radius) and MA2 (framing constant) are also disclosed assumptions but are not swept in sensitivity_model.py's FLEX[]/continuous-metric sense: MA1 gates a pass/fail wall-clearance check (see sensitivity_model.py's clip_radius CAVEAT print, not the FLEX sweep -- a +50% flex alone would fail Option B's BASE-case clipping check) and MA2 is a verified structural invariant (any flex scales both rigs' frame percentages by the same factor and leaves the margin exactly unchanged -- see sensitivity_model.py's framing_k invariance check and FACILITATOR.md's Argument for A). Neither needs an F/X/I disclosure entry because neither is an instability in the P5 sense.

balance.argument_a: The Fixed-Radius Orbit's cost structure is cheap and does not change no matter how the framing constant or the push-in depth are argued about -- it evaluates the same two trig terms every frame regardless. On tonight's stated numbers (Appendix B-D), it wins the graded ratio (percent-of-frame per millisecond) by 3.71%: 833.33 vs 803.55. The Variable-Radius Push-In's flashier single-frame telegraph shot (25.00% of frame vs 16.67%) does not survive being averaged honestly across the whole orbit (17.68% average) and divided by its own higher per-frame cost.
balance.argument_b: The Variable-Radius Push-In genuinely frames the boss better everywhere it matters most -- its worst frame (12.5% at the far side of the orbit) is still respectable, and its telegraph-moment frame (25.00%) is 50% better than the Fixed-Radius Orbit ever achieves. It also survives the arena's clipping check with room to spare in the base case (minimum radius 12 vs an 8.5-unit clipping limit). If the animation team wants even a modest increase in dramatic push-in depth (Appendix E, MA6), the Push-In wins outright -- exactly what the Twist demonstrates.
balance.margin_basis: Compare average percent-of-frame occupied (Appendix D's framing formula applied to Appendix B's governing equations, averaged over the 8 sampled orbit angles) divided by each rig's per-frame compute cost (Appendix D). Base case: A = 833.33, B = 803.55, A wins by 3.71%.
balance.twist_effect: Widening the push-in amplitude from 6 to 9 game-units (a +50% flex of MA6, framed in FACILITATOR.md as the animation team wanting a more dramatic push-in) raises Option B's average frame percentage from 17.68% to 19.25% with no change in per-frame cost, flipping the ratio: B = 874.82 vs A's unchanged 833.33, a 4.98% win for B. The same change also shrinks Option B's clipping clearance from 3.5 game-units (12 - 8.5) to just 0.5 game-units (9 - 8.5) -- the rig barely still clears the wall.
